title: Complete syllogistic proof registers with independently grounded pictorial arguments
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, NOT SELECTED: read complete passages as explicit proof traces in a fixed historical categorical calculus, with term arguments bound to independently observed classes and witnesses. Logical derivability and countermodels supply constraints beyond string grammar or anonymous graph matching. The four categorical forms and medieval transformations are documented in The Syllogism and Its Transformations (Cambridge History of Medieval Logic, chapter 12); the exact historical calculus and existential-import convention must still be frozen. GDT395 warns that successful internal structure does not identify meanings. No target, image or control was inspected, and no logical Voynich provenance is claimed.

design.mechanism: The source language contains A(S,P), E(S,P), I(S,P), O(S,P), respectively class inclusion, disjointness, nonempty intersection and a witnessed S outside P. Its complete inference set is Barbara: A(M,P),A(S,M) -> A(S,P); Celarent: E(M,P),A(S,M) -> E(S,P); Darii: A(M,P),I(S,M) -> I(S,P); Ferio: E(M,P),I(S,M) -> O(S,P). Every term must have an independently observed member, fixing existential import uniformly. Each complete group is one assertion with its term addresses or one of these four inferences with references to prior assertion indices, serialized with fixed separators and canonical decimal addresses under one global injective symbol key. A passage starts only from independently supplied premises, includes every intermediate assertion needed by its recorded rules and ends at an independently designated conclusion. No new unobserved premise, flexible term definition, rule addition, dropped group or per-passage key is allowed. Historical evidence for this compact serialization is currently missing.
design.unit: An entire proof and all of its premises, steps and conclusion. Term registers refer to independently designated classes of pictured objects; existential premises require identifiable witnesses. Register names carry no guessed botanical or anatomical word meanings.
design.contrast: A complete proof imposes a fixed consequence relation and admits explicit countermodels; an incidence graph or freely relabeled predicate inventory does not. The global quantifier key must satisfy every proof and independently observed class membership. Permuting empty predicates or dualizing ungrounded classes can preserve validity, so proof grammar alone cannot bind A, E, I and O to their proposed meanings. Independent positive and negative membership facts are needed to break those symmetries.
design.prediction: Freeze the calculus, key and class bindings on whole proofs, then decode a separately designated complete proof with independently specified premises before inspecting its conclusion or witness configuration. Every surviving decoder must predict the same final relation. A proof step with a finite countermodel, a conclusion false in the independently observed configuration, or an existential conclusion without the required witness refutes the corresponding full reading. If the premises, conclusion ownership or class memberships were inferred from the candidate text itself, this is only an internal proof parse and cannot be scored as meaning.
design.scope: Potential complete relational reading, not recovery of unique original wording or named species. No currently authenticated premise/conclusion bindings, class-membership census or historical proof-register notation is available. Selection requires a real fixed historical calculus and an independently grounded complete argument with a non-vacuous predicted conclusion. Historical reference: https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/73A6C0ACF0C9047B63FB319B302A9C2C/9781107449862c12_p290-315_CBO.pdf/the-syllogism-and-its-transformations.pdf . This raw architecture grants no new semantic value or relation-edge admission.
